title: How good is a hash?
description:
Compare hash functions by how evenly they fill buckets.

```
1000 words into 64 buckets
sum of letters:   biggest bucket 61, empty 23
FNV-1a:           biggest bucket 26, empty 0
std::hash:        biggest bucket 27, empty 0
```
hints: FNV-1a: start with `14695981039346656037ULL`; for each byte, `h ^= byte; h *= 1099511628211ULL;` (lesson 2.02).
Write one `report(name, hashFunction)` that takes a function so you do not repeat the counting.
requirements: Three hash functions on `std::string`: the sum of the characters, FNV-1a (64-bit) and `std::hash`.
Generate 1000 different words (for example `"word" + std::to_string(i)`) and count how many land in each of 64 buckets.
Print the largest bucket and the number of empty ones for each; your numbers will differ.
stretch: Show that "sum of letters" gives the same hash for anagrams like `listen` and `silent`.
